items.title: BRICS agrees on joint declaration before New Delhi summit, sources say
items.author: Sarita Singh, Shivangi Acharya, Saurabh Sharma
items.creator: Sarita Singh, Shivangi Acharya, Saurabh Sharma
items.summary: The BRICS group of emerging economies has agreed on a joint declaration, sources told Reuters on Saturday, hours before its leaders began a summit in New Delhi, aiming to boost the bloc's global clout.
items.body:
The BRICS group of emerging economies has agreed on a joint declaration, sources told Reuters on Saturday, hours before its leaders began a summit in New Delhi, aiming to boost the bloc's global clout.
The summit, hoping to bridge divisions between members Iran and the United Arab Emirates over the Gulf conflict, is being held as the United States and Iran resume [USN:L6N45203X TEXT:"tit-for-tat strikes"] in their six-month-old war.
That followed a pause in fighting for much of August, while the Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in Yemen [USN:L6N453173 TEXT:"tightened their grip"] in the Red Sea region.
Negotiators had agreed on a joint declaration unlikely to name any country but which will condemn unilateral war by any country, four sources told Reuters, adding that the bloc's leaders were expected to approve the document later on Saturday.
The foreign ministry of host India did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the declaration.
Foreign policy experts had said the key test for the bloc would be finding language on the Middle East crisis that both Abu Dhabi and Tehran could accept, clearing the way for a joint declaration.
Such a joint statement was unlikely to influence the current geopolitical landscape, but would demonstrate unity by a grouping of emerging nations against economically debilitating policies such as Western sanctions, they said.
BRICS [USN:FWN41R1LK TEXT:"foreign ministers"] meeting in New Delhi in May were unable to issue a joint statement, stymied by differences between Iran and the UAE.
BLOC SEEKS TO RAISE INTERNATIONAL PROFILE The BRICS bloc is seeking to raise its profile by influencing international rules and demanding the reform of institutions such as the World Bank, IMF and WTO, which some members view as being dominated by Western powers.
Leaders attending the summit are Russian President Vladimir Putin, China's Xi Jinping, Iran's Masoud Pezeshkian, South Africa's Cyril Ramaphosa and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, among others.
New Delhi, which has strong ties with the United States, Russia, Israel, Iran and the Gulf Arab states is engaged in a diplomatic balancing act, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi pushing BRICS members to boost trade cooperation, reduce barriers, and expand business opportunities.
The need to bridge the Iran-UAE divide over the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and produce a consensus summit declaration, however, has been an immediate concern for BRICS diplomats and officials.
UAE, after being hit by Iranian missiles since the war began, suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran in August.
BRICS groups Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates.
It was [USN:L6N4510UT TEXT:"set up"] in 2009 to challenge a world order dominated by the United States and its Western allies. Together, its members account for more than 40% of the world's population and almost a quarter of the global economy.
items.raw_description: The BRICS group of emerging economies has agreed on a joint declaration, sources told Reuters on Saturday, hours before its leaders began a summit in New Delhi, aiming to boost the bloc's global clout.

items.title: Pirates ace Paul Skenes hopes for better outcome vs. Cubs
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Alex Bregman has been heating up since the All-Star break, and Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell couldn't be happier.
items.body:
Alex Bregman has been heating up since the All-Star break, and Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell couldn't be happier.
The three-time All-Star will look to continue his hot hitting on Saturday afternoon as the Cubs chase a series victory against the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates.
Bregman belted a two-run homer and finished a triple shy of the cycle on Friday afternoon, helping Chicago cruise to a 12-2 romp over Pittsburgh in the opener of a three-game series. The homer was Bregman's 25th of the season and 16th since the All-Star break.
"It's kind of been a tale of two halves for him. And that's just the way it is this year," Counsell said. "We're glad the second half is going this way, and we have some games to go with him playing like this. He's had an Alex Bregman season. ... He's doing what we'd hoped he would do."
Bregman wasn't the only one to swing a hot bat on Friday.
Michael Busch drove in three runs and Seiya Suzuki scored three runs and joined Bregman with three hits for the Cubs (82-66), who banged out 16 hits en route to snapping a four-game skid.
Chicago is tied with the Philadelphia Phillies (82-66) for the National League's top wild-card spot.
The Cubs are expected to be tested on Saturday afternoon against reigning NL Cy Young Award winner Paul Skenes (10-11, 3.83 ERA).
Skenes scattered four hits over 5 1/3 scoreless innings in a 1-0 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday. The win was the first for the right-hander since July 19, ending a seven-outing winless run.
Skenes has struggled in two starts versus the Cubs this season, going 0-2 with a 5.06 ERA. All told, he is 2-4 with a 3.45 ERA in nine career appearances (all starts) against Chicago.
Cubs right-hander Clay Holmes (6-7, 2.83 ERA) is expected to get the nod on Saturday.
Holmes strung together four consecutive strong outings before getting shelled for eight runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings of a 10-3 setback to the Miami Marlins on Sunday.
Holmes, a former Pirate, is 0-1 with a 4.22 ERA in six career appearances (one start) versus Pittsburgh.
Rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin tripled and singled on Friday for the Pirates (74-74), who likely will be without Esmerlyn Valdez. The rookie right fielder left the Friday game in the sixth inning due to left hamstring discomfort.
Valdez's departure came on the same day that Pittsburgh welcomed back Ryan O'Hearn, who was activated off the 10-day injured list. He had been sidelined since July 31 with a left quad injury.
"You love when guys want to push it to get back and just to make sure that he's in a good spot to be able to do that," Pirates manager Don Kelly said of O'Hearn, who went 0-for-2 on Friday after entering the game as a pinch hitter.
"Confident in him being able to be Ryan O'Hearn and have good at-bats and be able to move around like he does."
Pirates rookie catcher Rafael Flores Jr. carries a career-best six-game hitting streak into the Saturday contest.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Philippines begins identifying victims from ferry fire as dozens still missing
items.author: Adrian Portugal, Eloisa Lopez
items.creator: Adrian Portugal, Eloisa Lopez
items.summary: Philippine authorities began the painstaking process of identifying victims from a ferry fire on Saturday, a day after responders recovered bodies from the burned-out vessel, raising the death toll to at least 35 and leaving more than 50 people missing.
items.body:
Philippine authorities began the painstaking process of identifying victims from a ferry fire on Saturday, a day after responders [USN:L6N45307E TEXT:"recovered bodies"] from the burned-out vessel, raising the death toll to at least 35 and leaving more than 50 people missing.
The bodies were transported to a port in Coron town, where temporary tents were set up for forensic teams to process and identify the victims.
Near the port, some family members anxiously watched as responders in protective suits carried black body bags from a Coast Guard vessel to temporary tents.
One of them was Anelyn Magbanua, 37, whose husband was returning to Coron after visiting their children in Manila when the ferry, which was carrying more than 130 people, caught fire near the end of its more than 20-hour journey.
"I hope he is not among the dead being brought off the ship. I hope he is alive and has only drifted to another island," she said.
"It will be very difficult to accept if he's really gone," she said. "He loved his children very much."
Firefighters entered the ferry for the first time on Friday after extinguishing the blaze more than a day after it broke out, giving authorities access to areas that had been hard to reach because of thick smoke and extreme heat. The Coast Guard said burnt remains were discovered in the ferry's economy accommodation section.
Images released by the Coast Guard showed the scale of the destruction inside the vessel, with rows of steel bed frames twisted by intense heat and blanketed in ash. Some photographs appeared to show skeletal remains among the debris.
Philippine Coast Guard official Geronimo Tuvilla said at a press conference on Saturday that the immediate priority was to identify the victims and determine the cause of the fire.
A statement from the Maritime Industry Authority, citing survivor accounts, said two explosions were heard inside the vessel shortly before the fire broke out.
One survivor interviewed by GMA News recalled seeing a small amount of smoke that turned into a fire and quickly spread through the ferry within seconds.
Questions also remained over the fate of the vessel's captain. Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said at the same press conference that she had received information that he was alive, but added that the captain's name was not on the list of 43 confirmed survivors.
The fire is the latest in a string of deadly maritime accidents in the Philippines, an archipelago of more than 7,600 islands where millions rely on ferries and small boats to travel between provinces and islands.

items.title: Taking AI too far? New Mexico Supreme Court fines lawyer $5,000 for presenting ‘fake testimony’, ChatGPT-generated brief
items.author: Swati Gandhi
items.summary: New Mexico Supreme Court fined a defence lawyer $5,000 for submitting a brief containing ‘fake police testimony’ and ‘fabricated witness statements’ generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT.
items.body: The New Mexico Supreme Court on Wednesday fined a defence lawyer $5,000 after he submitted a brief containing fake police testimony and fabricated witness statements generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT.Stephen Aarons, a defence lawyer representing a client in an appeal against a murder conviction, was held in contempt for failing to verify the accuracy of the filing. He said he prepared the brief with the help of the artificial intelligence (AI) programme, Reuters reported.Here's what happenedAarons, a private attorney from Santa Fe, was representing Oscar Renee Sandoval in his appeal. Sandoval had pleaded not guilty to killing the mother of his children but was convicted and sentenced to life in prison last year.Last month, the New Mexico Supreme Court asked Aarons to explain how the fabricated material, which reportedly contained details such as “fictional statements that the shooter was wearing dark pants and a white shirt,” came to be included in his main appeal brief.At a hearing on 21 August, the private attorney told the panel that he uploaded a computer-generated transcript and other case materials to ChatGPT, assuming that the AI chatbot would generate "a bulletproof summary."After hearing his explanation, the judges expressed disbelief that he was not fully aware of AI’s potential to make mistakes. Justice C Shannon Bacon said, "Counsel, do you watch the news? Do you listen to the radio? Do you read anything about what's going on in the world?" and added, "Because the problem with lawyers relying on AI hallucinations is an above-the-fold story every single day.”In a statement, the defence lawyer said that when he agreed to take up the defendant's case last year, he used ChatGPT, OpenAI's chatbot, to summarise the trial proceedings. However, he said he did not understand the degree to which the chatbot could "hallucinate" facts.He said, "I am remorseful but hopeful that the disciplinary board takes into account it was an honest mistake," and added, "It is a lesson learned for all professionals who rely upon this powerful but sometimes unstable technology."Aarons' case comes at a time when courts across the United States are seeing a growing number of cases in which lawyers have been disciplined by both state and federal judges for using AI tools without properly vetting their court documents before submitting them. According to the report, some judges have also faced scrutiny over their own use of AI.Additionally, several lawyers have faced sanctions for submitting briefs containing AI-generated errors, including fake case citations and incorrect references to the law. Aarons’ filing appears to have taken the issue a step further, with fabricated witness testimony included in a criminal appeal.What did the court say?The court said that the filing "contained false testimony from wholly fabricated witnesses," and added that Aarons had “demonstrated a lack of remorse and a lack of concern for his client.” The panel also noted that Aarons will be referred to an attorney disciplinary board for further investigation.The appeal, which is still pending, was assigned to Kim Chavez Cook, a New Mexico public defender, earlier this month.(with inputs from Reuters)

items.title: Andrew Sears set to rejoin Tigers for start against Rockies
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Detroit Tigers traded a two-time Cy Young Award-winning pitcher and tumbled out of the playoff race last month. A jolt of youth and energy has given them hope for the future.
items.body:
The Detroit Tigers traded a two-time Cy Young Award-winning pitcher and tumbled out of the playoff race last month. A jolt of youth and energy has given them hope for the future.
Detroit, which hosts the Colorado Rockies on Saturday afternoon in the second game of a three-game series, has won four of its last six games.
Infielder Kevin McGonigle appears headed for the American League Rookie of the Year award, and center fielder Max Clark is among numerous prospects getting extended playing time as the season winds down.
Clark belted a solo homer on Friday and scored another run after getting hit by a pitch. He stole second, then reached third and home on wild pitches in Detroit's 6-2, series-opening victory.
"When you see him running in open speed, he's top-tier speed," manager A.J. Hinch said. "And he's going to learn how to use it and trust that he can do even more than what he's doing now. And that's exciting."
Another rookie, left-hander Andrew Sears (0-1, 4.38 ERA), is expected to be recalled from Triple-A Toledo to make a spot start for Detroit on Saturday. He will be facing the Rockies for the first time.
Sears was optioned after his first career start on Sept. 4, when he held the Cleveland Guardians to one run and four hits in 5 2/3 innings during a no-decision.
"Definitely felt good," he said after that contest. "I was back in my own routine and in my element. Definitely just attacked it like any other start."
And Sears likes to attack quickly. He wastes little time between pitches.
"It just keeps the hitters dialed in," he said. "They don't like working fast. They're trying to use the clock against me. But as soon as they look at me, I'm throwing the ball."
Sears is 3-2 with a 2.16 ERA in 16 games, including 12 starts, in the minors this season. He is a candidate to win a starting job with the Tigers next spring.
"He can handle the moment and the responsibility," Hinch said. "(The Sept. 4 start) was even more impressive because he knew going into the game he was going to be leaned on quite a bit. It's the most pitches he's thrown this year, and he knew he had to carry the lion's share of the workload."
Right-hander Tanner Gordon (1-4, 5.40 ERA) will get the ball for the Rockies. He will be making his 10th start to go with 12 long-relief stints. Gordon has pitched at least three innings in all but one of his appearances this season.
After giving up just one run in each of his last two August starts, Gordon was rocked for five runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings by the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday.
He is 0-2 with a 10.24 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers.
The Rockies, who have lost five straight, produced 10 hits during the series opener but left nine men on base. Zac Veen, who finished 1-for-2 after entering in the seventh inning, drove in a ninth-inning run with an infield hit.
"I like doing whatever I can to help the team win," said Veen, who comes off the bench more than he starts. "Every game you might get one or two moments to make an impact."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Yankees look to continue offensive surge against rival Mets
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The New York Yankees are starting to get going on offense, and they hope to continue their productivity at the plate Saturday afternoon when they host the New York Mets.
items.body:
The New York Yankees are starting to get going on offense, and they hope to continue their productivity at the plate Saturday afternoon when they host the New York Mets.
The Yankees (85-62) are 17-7 in their past 24 games and enter Saturday three games behind the first-place Tampa Bay Rays (88-59) in the American League East and 5 1/2 games ahead of the Boston Red Sox (80-68) for the AL's top wild-card spot.
After totaling 13 hits on Friday in a 6-4 win over the Mets following a pregame ceremony to mark the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks, the Yankees are hitting .264 with 31 homers while scoring 126 runs in their past 24 games.
The Yankees have totaled 27 runs and 39 hits during a four-game winning streak that coincides with Aaron Judge's return from a fractured right rib that cost him 84 games. The Yankees went 45-39 in his absence.
"I'm encouraged," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "For much of the season offensively, from that kind of middle of the season until a few weeks ago, no hiding it, it was a grind for us. A couple of months of really struggling. We're winning games but on the strength of just doing winning things late.
"So I do feel like we're finding our stride a little bit offensively. Obviously we're a lot more whole now with not only getting Aaron but a couple of other guys back in the mix, and I feel like there's a lot of different places we can hurt you in the lineup now and we need to keep that going, but it does feel like we're building to a good place offensively."
Cody Bellinger hit a three-run homer for the Yankees on Friday and Ben Rice added a solo shot as both players continued their hot streaks.
Bellinger is hitting .377 (20-for-53) in his past 13 games while Rice is batting .338 (23-for-68) in his past 17.
The Mets (68-79) scored 35 runs during a four-game winning streak that included a 15-14 win over the Miami Marlins on Wednesday. However, they were held to seven hits and went 1-for-6 with runners in scoring position in the opener at Yankee Stadium.
Juan Soto struck out twice and also hit into a game-ending double play. He finished 1-for-5, and he has six hits in his past 30 at-bats (.200). Francisco Lindor is in a 5-for-28 (.179) slump after lining out with the bases loaded in the seventh and going 1-for-5.
Mets rookie A.J. Ewing is hitting .545 (12-for-22) in his past six games after homering. He also has reached base safely in 10 straight games.
"I thought the ceremony was great and I thought it was super cool to see the fans get together for it," Ewing said.
Gerrit Cole (8-8, 3.41 ERA) starts for the Yankees on Saturday, hoping to avoid a repeat of his 4-3 loss at San Diego on Sunday. He allowed three straight homers to the Padres' Fernando Tatis Jr., Jake Cronenworth and Manny Machado to start the first inning.
Cole later served up a solo shot to Luis Campusano. He permitted four runs on six hits while completing seven innings, tied for his longest outing of the season.
The right-hander is 2-4 with a 6.99 ERA in nine career starts against the Mets.
Mets left-hander Zac Thornton (3-5, 3.53 ERA) will make his 13th career start and first against the Yankees. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 10 starts but is coming off yielding six runs on seven hits, including four homers, in five innings during a 9-5 loss to the San Francisco Giants on Sept. 5.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Sebi proposes changes to derivatives settlement, closing auction timings
items.author: Khushboo Tiwari
items.summary: The regulator has floated two expiry-day settlement methodologies, two alternatives for market timings and changes to order cancellation and Iceberg orders during CAS ...
items.body: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has proposed changes to the settlement methodology for derivatives, market timings and certain operational aspects of the closing auction session (CAS), weeks after the new closing price mechanism came into effect. Under the proposals, settlement prices for index and single-stock derivatives on expiry days could either continue to be based on the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) of trades in the last 30 minutes of continuous trading, or move to a blended methodology that takes into account trades during the last 30 minutes of continuous trading and 10 minutes of CAS. Sebi has also proposed that exchanges stop disseminating the indicative index value (IIV) derived from indicative equilibrium prices (IEPs) during CAS, while continuing to provide security-level IEPs. The regulator said such index values may be misinterpreted as actual levels reached by the index. On market timings, Sebi has put forward two alternatives. Under Option A, continuous trading in CAS stocks would continue until 3:30 pm, followed by the auction, with derivatives trading continuing until 3:45 pm. Under Option B, the existing 3:15 pm cut-off for continuous trading in CAS stocks would remain, while derivatives trading would end at 3:30 pm. The regulator has also proposed reducing the transition period between continuous trading and CAS from five minutes to up to one minute and cutting the post-CAS derivatives trading window from 10 minutes to five minutes. It has proposed restricting cancellation of orders placed more than 1 per cent away from the reference price, while allowing price-improving modifications. Unexecuted Iceberg orders at the start of CAS could also be converted into normal limit orders, with the entire pending quantity disclosed. The proposals are part of a consultation paper issued on Saturday. Sebi has invited public comments by October 3. CAS was introduced in the equity cash segment for stocks having derivatives contracts from August 3, 2026. Before CAS, the closing price was determined using the VWAP of trades executed during the last 30 minutes of continuous trading. Under CAS, the closing price is determined through an equilibrium price discovery mechanism based on buy and sell orders accumulated in the auction book. However, derivatives continue to trade while the underlying securities go through the closing price discovery process. Sebi said this assumes particular significance on expiry days, when derivatives activity can be concentrated towards the close and participants may respond to evolving prices of the underlying securities during CAS. The initial experience has shown that derivatives activity remains significant immediately before and around CAS. Sebi also noted that participants were taking into account IEP information during CAS, particularly in the initial few minutes, while making decisions in derivatives contracts. An IEP, however, is not an executed traded price. It is an evolving price based on orders in the auction book and can change as orders are added, modified or cancelled. Against this backdrop, Sebi has proposed two settlement options. Under Option 1, or Blended VWAP, the expiry-day settlement price for both index and stock derivatives would use trades executed during the last 30 minutes of continuous trading and the 10 minutes of CAS. For index derivatives, the contribution of the two periods would be determined by their actual traded value, with no predetermined weight assigned to either period. For stock derivatives, the blended price would similarly be determined using VWAP across exchanges, taking into account actual traded value during the last 30 minutes of continuous trading and 10 minutes of CAS. Under Option 2, or CTS VWAP, the settlement price would initially continue to be based only on trades executed during the last 30 minutes of continuous trading, as was the case before CAS. CAS transactions would not form part of the settlement calculation during this interim period. Sebi said the CTS VWAP approach could be retained for at least one year before considering a transition to the blended methodology. Such a transition would not be automatic and would depend on factors including liquidity and participation in CAS, participant familiarity with the mechanism and an assessment of its price-discovery characteristics under different market conditions. Sebi has proposed continuing the dissemination of security-level IEPs but stopping the dissemination of an IEP-derived IIV for indices during CAS. The regulator said an index itself does not participate in the auction. Its indicative value during CAS is derived from the evolving IEPs of its constituent securities. The final index value is established only after the auction concludes and final prices of the constituent securities are determined. Thus, if an index’s IIV moves from 50,000 to 48,500 during CAS, it does not mean the index actually traded or reached 48,500. Sebi said such movements may nevertheless be misconstrued by market participants as actual index levels. The consultation paper notes that international closing auction mechanisms generally distinguish between indicative prices for securities participating in the auction and the calculation of index values. The review cited by Sebi found that unexecuted indicative prices of constituent securities are generally not used for continuously recalculating the corresponding disseminated index value during a closing auction. Sebi has proposed shortening the transition period between continuous trading and CAS from five minutes to up to one minute. The regulator said this would reduce the transition period while retaining time for exchanges to complete operational processes required to start CAS. Under Option A, continuous trading for all stocks would run until 3:30 pm. After a transition period of about one minute, CAS would run from 3:31 pm to 3:40 pm for CAS stocks. Derivatives trading would continue until 3:45 pm. Under Option B, continuous trading for CAS stocks would continue until 3:15 pm, while non-CAS stocks would continue to trade until 3:30 pm. CAS would run from 3:15 pm to 3:25 pm, including a transition period of about one minute, and derivatives trading would end at 3:30 pm. Under both options, the reference price used for determining the CAS price band would continue to be based on the VWAP of trades during the last 15 minutes of continuous trading. Sebi has also proposed reducing the post-CAS derivatives window to five minutes. The existing 10-minute window was intended, among other things, to allow funds to achieve end-of-day exposures and arbitrageurs to square off unmatched positions. For single-stock derivatives, it also provides an opportunity to manage physical delivery obligations. Restrictions proposed on cancellations, Iceberg orders The existing CAS price band of plus or minus 3 per cent would remain unchanged. Instead of narrowing the band, Sebi has proposed a targeted restriction on cancellations. Orders placed within 1 per cent of the reference price could continue to be cancelled. But orders placed at, or modified to, prices beyond 1 per cent and up to 3 per cent from the reference price would not be allowed to be cancelled during CAS. They could, however, be modified to improve the price, subject to the overall 3 per cent band. Sebi said the approach is intended to reduce the scope for withdrawal of trading interest materially away from the reference price while retaining the ability of participants to improve their orders as demand and supply conditions evolve. The regulator has also proposed allowing unexecuted Iceberg orders to move from continuous trading into CAS. The pending quantity would be converted into a normal limit order and the entire unexecuted quantity would be disclosed in the CAS order book. Sebi said this would ensure that eligible trading interest outstanding at the end of continuous trading can participate in the closing auction and that the quantity available for execution is fully reflected in the auction order book. The regulator has sought comments on all seven proposals by October 3, 2026.

items.title: Meloni sees Italy 2026 growth at 1%, matching euro zone
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expects Italy's economy to grow by 1% this year, in line with the euro zone, she said in an interview with newspaper Il Foglio published on Saturday.
items.body:
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expects Italy's economy to grow by 1% this year, in line with the euro zone, she said in an interview with newspaper Il Foglio published on Saturday.
Meloni's government in April forecast 2026 gross domestic product growth of 0.6%, but budget watchdog UPB last month issued a [USN:L8N4410YQ TEXT:"more upbeat projection"] of 0.9%.
"The Italian economy is holding up well, and data from the first six months of the year could point to 2026 growth of 1%, in line with, if not above, that of the euro zone," Meloni told Il Foglio.
Italian GDP rose by 0.3% quarter-on-quarter in January to March and by 0.2% in the second quarter.
So-called "acquired growth" stood at 0.8% at the end of June, meaning that even if GDP is flat in each of the remaining two quarters of 2026, full-year growth will be up 0.8% from 2025.
"It is also true that the Italian economy has struggled for many years to achieve sustained and steady growth," Meloni added, citing energy costs and low productivity among the reasons.
"We are working to address these issues, but the results of those efforts will only become visible over the medium term," she said.
The Italian economy grew 0.5% in 2025.
It hasn't exceeded 1% in the last three years despite the steady influx of tens of billions of euros of COVID-19 recovery funds from the European Union.

items.title: Ford to recall about 223,500 US vehicles over fuel tank issues
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ford is recalling 223,472 vehicles in the U.S. due to leaky and improperly secured fuel tanks that may detach from the vehicle while driving, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Saturday.
items.body:
Ford (F.N) is recalling 223,472 vehicles in the U.S. due to leaky and improperly secured fuel tanks that may detach from the vehicle while driving, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Saturday.
Here are some more details from the NHTSA advisory:
A detached tank can create a road hazard, increasing the risk of a crash, while a fuel leak can cause an engine stall or increase the risk of a fire.
Certain 2023-2027 F-150 vehicles will be recalled due to this concern.
Dealers will inspect and replace the fuel tank straps, as necessary, free of charge.

items.title: India's markets regulator proposes revamp of derivatives expiry pricing
items.author: Jayshree Pyasi, Vivek M
items.creator: Jayshree Pyasi, Vivek M
items.summary: India's markets regulator proposed on Saturday a review of how settlement prices for index and stock derivatives are determined on expiry day.
items.body:
India's markets regulator proposed on Saturday a review of how settlement prices for index and stock derivatives are determined on expiry day.
The plans were unveiled in a consultation paper laying out changes to the newly launched Closing Auction Session (CAS) that has led to sharp [USN:L4N44S0W8 TEXT:"market swings"] on derivatives expiry days.
The CAS framework was introduced in the equity cash segment for stocks on which derivatives contracts are available, with effect from August 3.
The move aimed at efficient and transparent discovery of the closing price of securities.
Here are details:
• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has floated two options for expiry-day settlement price of index and stock derivatives.
• The first option would blend trades from the last 30 minutes of normal trading with the 10-minute closing auction to yield the settlement price.
• The second option would go back to using only the last 30 minutes of normal trading, leaving out the closing auction from the calculation altogether, at least for a year.
• The second option would effectively de-link derivatives settlement from CAS for at least a year
• The other proposals include barring cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1% above or below the reference price, reducing to five minutes from ten the post-closing auction window for derivatives trading, and not disseminating indicative index close levels during the closing auction.
• The regulator has proposed to continue disseminating indicative equilibrium price for stocks during the closing auction.
• The regulator invited submission of public comments on the proposals by October 3.
• "SEBI is not backing away from CAS. Instead, it is trying to refine CAS after observing expiry-day behaviour," said Rajesh Palviya, senior vice president and head of research at Axis Securities.
• "The key objective is to reduce the disconnect between cash-market price discovery and derivatives trading near the close," Palviya said.

items.title: MLB roundup: Rays, Brewers become first teams to clinch playoff berths
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Junior Caminero launched a mammoth walk-off home run in the ninth inning Friday night, sending the Tampa Bay Rays to the postseason by virtue of a 3-1 win over the Houston Astros in St. Petersburg, Fla.
items.body:
Junior Caminero launched a mammoth walk-off home run in the ninth inning Friday night, sending the Tampa Bay Rays to the postseason by virtue of a 3-1 win over the Houston Astros in St. Petersburg, Fla.
The American League's home run leader, Caminero crushed a 417-foot blast to left-center field off reliever Bryan Abreu (6-4) for his 40th long ball. One batter earlier, Jonathan Aranda nearly homered to right-center, settling for a one-out double.
Caminero then belted Abreu's 97 mph first-pitch fastball for his first career walk-off blast, making the Rays the first club to clinch a postseason spot this year. The Milwaukee Brewers joined them a short time later.
Drew Rasmussen drew a no-decision after seven strong innings, though the Rays won for the 10th consecutive time in games he has started. The AL West-leading Astros outhit the Rays 9-4. Yainer Diaz went 2-for-3 with an RBI and a walk.
Brewers 20, Reds 0
Garrett Mitchell hit a grand slam, William Contreras homered and drove in six runs, and Dustin May tossed six innings of two-hit ball as Milwaukee routed visiting Cincinnati to clinch its eighth postseason berth in nine seasons.
The Brewers fell short of the biggest shutout in modern major league history, a record they tied on Aug. 18 by trouncing the Seattle Mariners 22-0. May (7-9) struck out six and walked one. Brice Turang (3-for-3, four RBIs) and Jake Bauers homered during a six-run second.
The Brewers jumped on Andrew Abbott (6-11) for two runs in the first and six in the second, ending his outing after he allowed nine hits. Sal Stewart collected the only two hits for the Reds, who have lost four straight.
Yankees 6, Mets 4
Carlos Rodon pitched 6 1/3 sharp innings and the host New York Yankees homered twice off rookie Nolan McLean in a victory over the New York Mets on the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.
The Yankees won for the ninth time in 12 games while moving closer to clinching their ninth postseason spot in the past 10 seasons. Cody Bellinger hit a tiebreaking three-run homer off McLean (11-9) in the second and Ben Rice added a leadoff blast in the fifth.
Rodon (6-3) allowed two runs, one earned, on three hits and finished with eight strikeouts. McLean allowed five runs and a career-high 10 hits in five innings. The Mets got a homer and an RBI single from rookie A.J. Ewing but had a four-game winning streak snapped.
Braves 6, Phillies 5 (11 innings)
Drake Baldwin lined a two-out RBI double to center field in the 11th to cap a two-run rally and lift Atlanta to a victory over visiting Philadelphia, giving the Braves some breathing room in the National League East.
Atlanta, trailing 5-4, tied the game on Ha-Seong Kim's two-out single and walked it off on Baldwin's double against Brooks Raley (5-6). Didier Fuentes (7-2) was the winning pitcher. Philadelphia had taken the lead in the top of the 11th on an RBI single by Luis Arraez.
The win allowed the Braves to extend their division lead over the Phillies to five games.
Guardians 5, Twins 2
Angel Martinez went 2-for-4 with a two-run home run, and Cleveland scored three runs in the top of the ninth inning to secure a win over Minnesota in Minneapolis.
Brayan Rocchio had a double and two RBIs for Cleveland in the opener of the three-game series. Travis Bazzana went 2-for-2 and scored twice for the Guardians, who hold a two-game lead over the Toronto Blue Jays for the American League's third and final wild-card spot.
Royce Lewis and Kaelen Culpepper tallied one RBI apiece for Minnesota. Twins reliever Yoendrys Gomez (2-3) gave up three runs on two hits in one-third of an inning.
Cardinals 7, White Sox 3
Rookie Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal each had three hits and drove in two runs for St. Louis in a victory against visiting Chicago.
Alec Burleson had two hits and two RBIs for the Cardinals. Jordan Walker had two hits and two runs for St. Louis, which snapped a three-game losing streak.
Chase Meidroth hit a pair of home runs for the White Sox, who lost their fourth straight game and had their AL Central lead trimmed to a half-game over the second-place Guardians. Randal Grichuk joined Meidroth in collecting two of Chicago's nine hits.
Dodgers 6, Marlins 2
Kyle Tucker went 3-for-3 with a grand slam and a season-high five RBIs to lead visiting Los Angeles past Miami for its eighth straight win.
Dodgers starter Blake Snell (4-1) struck out eight in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed one run on four hits. Max Muncy added three hits for Los Angeles, and Will Smith contributed an RBI single.
Marlins starter Ryan Gusto (1-5) lasted six innings and held the Dodgers to two runs on five hits. Miami's offense was led by Otto Lopez, who went 4-for-5.
Nationals 4, Angels 3
Jorbit Vivas hit a tiebreaking two-run double to cap a three-run eighth inning as host Washington snapped a seven-game losing streak with a comeback victory over Los Angeles.
CJ Abrams had two hits and a run and James Wood had an RBI single and a walk for Washington. Clayton Beeter (6-5) tossed a scoreless eighth, and Erik Tolman earned his second save despite allowing a run.
Mike Trout hit a home run and Christian Moore doubled and had two hits and two RBIs for the Angels, who finished with just four hits. Los Angeles reliever Samy Natera Jr. (1-2) allowed three runs on three hits in one inning.
Padres 7, Giants 5
Dustin Harris and Freddy Fermin, the bottom two batters in the order, combined for four hits and four RBIs, Jackson Merrill chipped in with a double and two singles, and visiting San Diego overcame a Rafael Devers grand slam to beat San Francisco.
Robbie Ray (12-8) threw five innings of five-run ball for the Padres, who maintained a half-game lead on the Arizona Diamondbacks for the third NL wild card. Mason Miller loaded the bases in the ninth but escaped for his 35th save.
Giants starter Anthony Molina (3-1) allowed seven runs and nine hits in three innings. San Francisco's Jonah Cox had two hits and two runs.
Diamondbacks 9, Rangers 1
Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado hit back-to-back homers in a five-run sixth inning, Ketel Marte doubled twice and drove in three runs, and Arizona topped Texas in Phoenix.
Gabriel Moreno had two hits and two RBIs and Ildemaro Vargas had two hits and drove in a run for the D-backs, who posted their major-league-best 44th comeback victory and have won five of their past six. Reliever Kevin Ginkel (6-4) got two outs for the win.
Joc Pederson had two of the Rangers' five hits, including an RBI double. MacKenzie Gore (8-11) was charged with four runs on five hits in four-plus innings.
Cubs 12, Pirates 2
Alex Bregman belted a two-run homer and Michael Busch drove in three runs, fueling host Chicago to a victory over Pittsburgh.
Chicago's Seiya Suzuki scored three runs and joined Bregman with three hits. Carson Kelly ripped a two-run double in the second inning for the Cubs, who banged out 16 hits en route to snapping a four-game losing streak.
Pittsburgh rookie Konnor Griffin tripled to lead off the game and came around to score on an RBI single by Oneil Cruz. Bryan Reynolds capped a nine-pitch at-bat with a homer in the sixth inning for the Pirates, whose four-game winning streak ended.
Royals 3, Red Sox 2
Kansas City scored three runs over the first three innings and let its pitching do the rest as the visitors held on to beat Boston.
Carter Jensen had two doubles and an RBI and Salvador Perez went 2-for-4 with an RBI to lead the Royals. Seth Lugo (7-8) scattered seven hits and struck out seven across five innings of two-run ball. Steven Cruz registered his seventh save with a 1-2-3 ninth.
Mickey Gasper homered and Wilyer Abreu went 2-for-4 with an RBI double for the Red Sox, who have lost three straight since a five-game winning streak. Sonny Gray (17-5) went six frames and allowed three runs on six hits.
Orioles 7, Blue Jays 4
Dylan Beavers socked a solo home run and had three RBIs as visiting Baltimore defeated Toronto.
Coby Mayo added a solo blast and Christian Encarnacion-Strand rapped out three hits for the Orioles, who have won three out of four. Chris Bassitt (7-5) tossed five-plus innings of two-run ball. Rico Garcia got the final out to earn his eighth save.
Brett Bateman hit his first major league homer, a two-run shot, for the Blue Jays, and Kazuma Okamoto added a solo homer and a double. Max Scherzer (2-8) completed five innings, allowing six runs and seven hits.
Tigers 6, Rockies 2
Dillon Dingler hit a two-run homer, Max Clark supplied a solo shot and Detroit pulled away to hand visiting Colorado its fifth straight loss.
Riley Greene contributed a single, a double and a triple and two RBIs for the Tigers. Framber Valdez (10-10) held the Rockies to one unearned run and six hits in six innings. Kenley Jansen got the final out for his 19th save as Detroit won for the fourth time in six games.
Colorado starter Mason Adams permitted one run and two hits in five innings. Mark Manfredi (1-2) gave up two runs while recording only two outs.
Athletics 6, Mariners 5 (10 innings)
Donovan Walton led off the bottom of the 10th inning with a two-run, walk-off homer to right as the Athletics recorded a dramatic victory over Seattle at West Sacramento, Calif.
Walton jumped all over a 1-1 sweeper from Eduard Bazardo (3-4) for his third hit of the night to give the A's their seventh victory in nine games. Lawrence Butler had three hits, including a two-run homer, for the Athletics.
Julio Rodriguez hit a run-scoring ground single with two outs in the top of the 10th to give Seattle a 5-4 lead prior to Walton's winning blast. Lazaro Montes delivered a pinch-hit, two-run blast for Seattle.
--Field Level Media

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Krystal Hu　Milana Vinn

[１１日 ロイター] -
items.body:

items.title: China's Xi lands in Delhi for BRICS summit and talks with Modi
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in the Indian capital on Saturday for the summit of leaders of the BRICS group of countries and talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian TV channels showed.
items.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in the Indian capital on Saturday for the summit of leaders of the BRICS group of countries and talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian TV channels showed.
The visit is Xi's [USN:L4N44V073 TEXT:"first to India in seven years"] and comes as the Asian neighbours [USN:L6N4500OX TEXT:"cautiously rebuild ties"] that were badly damaged after a military clash on their disputed Himalayan border in 2020 in which 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed.
Xi stepped out of his plane to a red carpet welcome and was greeted by women performing traditional Indian dances.
The Xi-Modi meeting, scheduled for Saturday evening, will be their third in three years, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry said on Friday.
China "is willing" to work together with India, to view two-way relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, properly manage differences, and be "good neighbours and friends, as well as mutually supportive partners," the spokesperson said.
BRICS includes Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates.
The summit is being held amid geopolitical tensions triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, the Russia-Ukraine war and the disruption they have caused to global energy, trade and transport.

items.title: Padres hold on to beat Giants, extend win streak to five
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Dustin Harris and Freddy Fermin, the bottom two batters in the order, combined for four hits and four RBIs, Jackson Merrill chipped in with a double and two singles, and the visiting San Diego Padres overcame a Rafael Devers grand slam to beat the San Francisco Giants 7-5 in the opener of a three-game series Friday night.
items.body:
Dustin Harris and Freddy Fermin, the bottom two batters in the order, combined for four hits and four RBIs, Jackson Merrill chipped in with a double and two singles, and the visiting San Diego Padres overcame a Rafael Devers grand slam to beat the San Francisco Giants 7-5 in the opener of a three-game series Friday night.
Robbie Ray (12-8) recorded a win in his return to San Francisco, helping the Padres (79-68) capture a fifth straight victory and remain a half-game ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks (79-69) in the duel for the final National League wild-card playoff spot.
After the Giants opened the scoring on a Bryce Eldridge RBI single in the first inning, the Padres took the lead in the second when Harris singled in a run and Fermin doubled in another.
San Diego appeared to break the game open with a five-run third in which Harris, with an RBI triple, and Fermin, with a run-scoring double, were involved again. Xander Bogaerts had the big hit of the uprising, a two-run double.
Giants starter Anthony Molina (3-1) was pulled at inning's end, having allowed seven runs and nine hits in three innings. He walked two and struck out four.
Yunior Marte kept the Giants in the game with five innings of shutout relief, allowing Devers' fifth-inning grand slam to get the hosts back in the game at 7-5. The homer was Devers' 36th of the year.
Ray turned the ball over to the Padres bullpen after five innings, during which he was charged with five runs on four hits and four walks. He struck out five.
Yuki Matsui, Adrian Morejon and Bradgley Rodriguez retained the two-run advantage with a scoreless inning of relief apiece, setting the stage in the ninth for Mason Miller, who loaded the bases with two outs before striking out Eldridge to secure his 35th save.
Rodriguez's eighth inning included a leadoff double by Eldridge and two challenges by catcher Fermin that turned balls into strikeouts.
Harris and Merrill scored twice apiece for the Padres, who collected five doubles and two triples among 12 hits.
Eldridge and Jonah Cox, who scored twice, had two hits apiece for the Giants (62-86), who were coming off a three-game home sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals.
--Field Level Media

items.title: トランプ氏、中国車の米国生産「構わない」　雇用が重要と指摘
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン １１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン １１日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１１日、議会や自動車メーカーからの反対の声が強いにもかかわらず、中国の自動車メーカーが米国で生産することに反対しないと述べた。

ＦＯＸニュース番組のインタビューで「もし中国が米国に進出して、ここで自動車を生産する工場を開設したいというなら、私は構わない」と発言。「日本もそうしているが、彼らはわれわれの国民を雇っている。重要なのはわれわれの国民を雇うということだ」と語った。

また、ワシントンでの米中首脳会談を控える中、中国車の米国販売を許可する計画があるといううわさについて「まったくのデマ」と一蹴。これまで中国車を米国から締め出してきたと述べた。

２０２５年初にバイデン前政権が導入した規制により、事実上、全ての中国自動車メーカーが米国で乗用車を販売または製造することが禁止されている。

items.title: Top 25 roundup: Austin Simmons, No. 23 Mizzou win Border War vs. Kansas
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Austin Simmons passed for three touchdowns and Robert Woodyard Jr. forced a pair of turnovers on consecutive possessions in the second half Friday night, leading No. 23 Missouri to a 38-21 victory over Kansas in Lawrence, Kan.
items.body:
Austin Simmons passed for three touchdowns and Robert Woodyard Jr. forced a pair of turnovers on consecutive possessions in the second half Friday night, leading No. 23 Missouri to a 38-21 victory over Kansas in Lawrence, Kan.
Donovan Olugbode and Cayden Lee finished with more than 100 yards receiving apiece and each caught a touchdown pass for Missouri (2-0), which won its fifth straight "Border War" matchup, a rivalry that began in 1891. Jamal Roberts contributed 125 rushing yards and a TD on 28 carries.
Austin Alexander had an 88-yard touchdown return on a blocked field goal for Kansas (1-1), which has lost both meetings with Mizzou in a series that has been played only twice -- both in the past two seasons -- since the Tigers moved to the Southeastern Conference in 2012.
Jayhawks quarterback Isaiah Marshall finished 13 of 30 for 168 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.
No. 24 Louisville 59, Villanova 13
Lincoln Kienholz passed for 332 yards, threw for two touchdowns and rushed for two more to lead the Cardinals to a win over the visiting Wildcats.
Lawayne McCoy caught three passes for 102 yards and a touchdown, Tre Richardson had seven grabs for 98 yards and Jaleel Skinner had 82 receiving yards and a touchdown catch for Louisville (1-1). Marquise Davis had two rushing scores and Braxton Jennings added a rushing and a receiving TD for the Cardinals, who outgained Villanova 635-253.
Villanova quarterback Pat McQuaide completed 18 of 31 passes for 166 yards and one touchdown. Ja'briel Mace had 73 receiving yards and a TD reception for the Wildcats (1-2).
No. 25 Virginia 59, Norfolk State 3
Beau Pribula threw three touchdown passes in the first quarter and the Cavaliers cruised to a victory over the Spartans in Charlottesville, Va.
Pribula completed 12 of 14 passes for 162 yards and one interception before sitting out the second half for Virginia (2-0). Backup Eli Holstein added two touchdown passes, and Jacquon Gibson made two touchdown catches.
Deljay Bailey finished 15 of 25 for 142 yards and two interceptions for Norfolk State, which was outgained 466-223. The FCS-level Spartans (1-2) fell to 2-13 under second-year head coach and former NFL star Michael Vick.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Explosion hits another weapons site in Bulgaria
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: An explosion caused a fire at a weapons storage site in central Bulgaria overnight, local media and officials said on Saturday, the second blaze at a munitions facility in the past few weeks.
items.body:
An explosion caused a fire at a weapons storage site in central Bulgaria overnight, local media and officials said on Saturday, the second blaze at a munitions facility in the past few weeks.
No one was reported injured in the blaze, which broke out near the village of Tsareva Livada and could be seen lighting up the night sky in videos broadcast locally.
“At the moment, the fire is on the territory of the storage base of the factory. It is moving from warehouse to warehouse," Gabrovo regional governor Kristina Sidorova told journalists in the early hours of Saturday.
Local media reported that the fire was at a site run by EMCO, which experienced an explosion at another facility last month, citing an EMCO company official. Reuters was not immediately able to reach EMCO for comment.
EMCO is run by Bulgarian arms trader Emilian Gebrev, who Bulgarian prosecutors allege was the target of past attacks on his facilities by Russian operatives.
In 2024, Bulgaria issued an arrest warrant for six Russian citizens accused of involvement in the destruction of EMCO arms depots that were storing munitions for export to Ukraine and Georgia between 2011 and 2020.
Prosecutors at the time said that they could reasonably assume links between the blasts in Bulgaria, an attempted poisoning of Gebrev in 2015, and munitions depot explosions in the Czech Republic in 2014.
Moscow has dismissed the allegations.

items.title: Pachuca golea como visitante al Atlante en torneo mexicano
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pachuca goleó el viernes como visitante al Atlante por 3-0 en el inicio de la octava jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
items.body:
Pachuca goleó el viernes como visitante al Atlante por 3-0 en el inicio de la octava jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
Con su tercer triunfo en el torneo, los "Tuzos" de Pachuca llegaron a 11 puntos para subir del duodécimo al noveno lugar general.
En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, Pachuca se adelantó a los 13 minutos con un disparo del venezolano Salomón Rondón que fue desviado por un zaguero del Atlante y dejó sin oportunidad de reaccionar al portero Óscar Jiménez.
Pachuca aumentó su ventaja a los 20 minutos cuando el brasileño Robert Kenedy metió el balón por el ángulo derecho con un zurdazo en la entrada del área.
El tercer gol del equipo visitante cayó a los 37 minutos con un potente disparo del neerlandés Oussama Idrissi con el que el balón pegó en el travesaño antes de que cayera dentro de la portería.
En los otros encuentros del viernes, Puebla venció por 1-0 como visitante a Necaxa con un gol del uruguayo Mathías Tomas, quien metió el balón por el ángulo derecho con un potente zurdazo desde fuera del área a los 93 minutos.
En tanto, Querétaro ganó por 1-0 en su visita a Tijuana con gol del argentino Mateo Coronel.
La jornada continuará el sábado con los partidos entre Toluca-Atlas, Monterrey-Tigres UANL y Cruz Azul-América.
El domingo, Guadalajara enfrentará a Pumas UNAM, mientras que Santos Laguna jugará ante Bravos de Ciudad Juárez.
La jornada se completará el lunes cuando León sea local ante el Atlético de San Luis.

Shelton beat compatriot Frances Tiafoe 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5 on Friday to book a final with German top seed Alexander Zverev and move closer to ending a 23-year American wait for a men's singles Grand Slam champion since Andy Roddick's triumph in New York.
The 23-year-old will also aim to become the first Black American man to capture the New York title since Arthur Ashe in 1968, but knows he must earn a first victory over Zverev in their sixth meeting.
"This whole tournament at this point has been unchartered territory," Shelton told reporters. "I'm in positions I've never been in before. I've beaten guys that I've never beaten before. I'm just excited to put it all out on the line.
"I can think about how cool this moment is and what I'm playing for. At the end of the day, I'm here in New York, I'm hanging out with my team, I'm with my homies playing a little bit of tennis and I've been able to downplay the moment well.
"I've got great people around me that keep me grounded and focused and humble, and I think these moments I want to cherish, I don't want to take lightly. But at the same time, it's very business-like the way I've been going about it."
While Shelton acknowledged the nerves that come with the biggest match of his career, he said the chance to test himself against the top seed on the sport's grandest stages on Sunday was something he was embracing.
"The nerves are always there," he added.
"It's something that you've got to lean into. The nerves are as much there in the first round for me as in the semis, and I'm sure the finals will be the same.
"It's something you've got to be able to overcome, but I'm having fun, you know? I'm playing against the number one seed, playing against a Grand Slam champion trying to get my first.
"It's a lot of reasons that this is an enjoyable moment for me. Knowing I can leave it all on court and push myself to the absolute limit ... and see what I can do is an exciting thought."

items.title: Spurs' Mudryk sidelined by injury after comeback from doping ban
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Tottenham Hotspur winger Mykhailo Mudryk injured his ankle in training, according to British media reports, with manager Roberto De Zerbi hoping the Ukraine international can return as soon as possible after this latest setback.
items.body:
Tottenham Hotspur winger Mykhailo Mudryk injured his ankle in training, according to British media reports, with manager Roberto De Zerbi hoping the Ukraine international can return as soon as possible after this latest setback.
The 25-year-old [USN:L1N44T14D TEXT:"joined Spurs on a season-long loan"] from rivals Chelsea on transfer deadline day and made his debut off the bench in last weekend's goalless [USN:L1N44X04B TEXT:"draw at Nottingham Forest"].
Mudryk is expected to be sidelined until after the international break, said the media reports.
Mudryk previously played under De Zerbi on Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk before joining Chelsea in January 2023. He struggled to establish himself at Stamford Bridge, however, and his career was put on hold after an adverse analytical finding for meldonium in an anti-doping test in 2024.
The Football Association handed him a four-year ban, but he appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport and his [USN:L6N43X13J TEXT:"suspension was later reduced"] following an agreement between the FA and the World Anti-Doping Agency.
"(With) Mudryk, it was a stupid injury and we hope he can come back as soon as possible. For him and for us," De Zerbi told reporters on Friday.
"For him because he suffered too much and for us because we lost an important player.
"He played 15 minutes in Nottingham, he played well, but it's in the normal process when one player doesn't play for a long time."
Mudryk made 73 appearances for Chelsea, scoring 10 goals and registering 11 assists before his move to Spurs.
Spurs have made a disappointing start to the season, taking just one point from their opening three Premier League matches to sit 17th in the table. They host Everton later on Saturday.

items.title: サウジ、ホルムズ迂回パイプラインの稼働停止　ドローン攻撃受け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アデン／ドバイ １２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[アデン／ドバイ １２日 ロイター] - サウジアラビアは、ホルムズ海峡の輸送停滞を回避する代替ルートの役割を果たしている東西石油パイプラインの稼働を停止した。イランの支援を受ける武装組織が活動するイラクから飛来したドローン（無人機）攻撃を受けた予防措置という。

船舶追跡会社やアナリストによると、同パイプラインの輸送量はここ数カ月、１日当たり４００万─５００万バレルとなっており、これは世界供給量の４─５％に相当する。

この攻撃はイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派が紅海での支配力を強めている最中に発生。トランプ米大統領はフーシ派への直接攻撃見送り、サウジ皇太子の要請を退けた。

サウジのエネルギー省によると、東西パイプラインは１０日午前、リヤドとメディナ地域で攻撃を受けた。

攻撃の責任者は今のところ不明。衛星画像には、メディナ南部のパイプライン沿いから黒煙が立ち上っている様子が映し出されていた。

サウジ外務省は、この攻撃により数人の負傷者が出ており、被害状況を調べていると述べた。輸出への影響については詳細を明らかにしなかった。

また、イラク首相からの要請を受け、現時点では報復を行わない方針だとしつつ、国益を守るために「必要なあらゆる措置を講じる」権利を留保すると付け加えた。

一方、イラク政府は攻撃を非難し、マイサン県での作戦を指揮していた軍司令官を解任。同県はイランが支援するシーア派武装組織が活動し、影響力を維持している地域と見なされている。

items.title: Syrian private airport plans spark outcry over mass graves, land rights
items.author: Feras Dalatey
items.creator: Feras Dalatey
items.summary: Syrian government plans to turn a former military airport in Damascus into a hub for private jets are raising alarm among rights groups and residents who say redevelopment could disturb suspected mass graves and override private land claims.
items.body:
Syrian government plans to turn a former military airport in Damascus into a hub for private jets are raising alarm among rights groups and residents who say redevelopment could disturb suspected mass graves and override private land claims.
Syria’s civil aviation authority said last week it was preparing to reclassify Mezzeh military airport for limited civilian use, focused on private and executive aviation, to complement Damascus International Airport, according to a report on Syria's state news agency, SANA. Rubble removal and infrastructure upgrades had already begun, the report said.
The project is emerging as a test of how Syria’s new authorities balance a [USN:L1N44L0PT TEXT:"drive to attract investment"] and redevelop state assets with two unresolved legacies of Assad’s family rule: the fate of tens of thousands of missing Syrians and property rights clouded by decades of expropriation.
NEW DOCUMENTS SHOW AIRPORT'S ROLE AS EXECUTION SITE Under ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad and his father Hafez, Mezzeh housed key branches of the powerful Air Force Intelligence Directorate, as well as numerous detention facilities where suspected government opponents were tortured, executed and subjected to enforced disappearance. Parts of the air base were used for presidential and other official flights.
Air Force Intelligence (AFI) documents recently obtained by the Syria Justice and Accountability Centre (SJAC), a U.S.-based Syrian-led human rights group, and shared exclusively with Reuters, show that senior Syrian military officials approved Mezzeh in 2012 as a site for carrying out executions of detainees sentenced to death by military field courts.
One document proposed moving executions from [USN:L8N3NA0UJ TEXT:"Sednaya"] — the country's most notorious prison at the time — to Mezzeh because it was a "closed security compound" close to Damascus. Subsequent correspondence discussed a firing range and later a hangar beside the runway as execution sites.
The documents, which underscore the central role of Mezzeh in the Assad-era security system, show officials ordered construction of a platform at the hangar, requested nylon rope and directed that the work be carried out under AFI supervision “in utmost secrecy.”
A 2025 [USN:L6N3PH0O2 TEXT:"investigation"] by SJAC identified two suspected grave sites linked to people who died in detention at Mezzeh, where it said more than 1,150 detainees died, some by execution and others from torture or maltreatment.
In a July 2025 letter seen by Reuters, SJAC provided Syria’s National Commission for Missing Persons with the coordinates of the two suspected graves inside the airport, urging authorities to prevent construction or excavation until the sites were investigated.
The commission told SJAC at the time that there were no construction or refurbishment plans for Mezzeh, SJAC told Reuters.
SJAC wrote to the commission again on September 8 after the redevelopment plans emerged, warning that excavation, rubble removal or other works could damage human remains and evidence crucial to identifying victims, according to a second letter seen by Reuters.
SJAC told Reuters it had not yet received a response to its second letter.
Amer Matar, founder of the Syria Prisons Museum, a Germany-based NGO documenting detention facilities including those at Mezzeh, said the planned works showed a lack of respect for Syrian families who still have no answers on the fate of loved ones detained under Assad.
"To construct a business airport on a site that may contain mass graves, without a thorough prior investigation, without site protection, without searching for the missing and their remains, and without preserving evidence, is an act of extreme recklessness and disregard," Matar told Reuters.
The Syrian civil aviation authority, Syria's National Commission for Missing Persons and Syria's defense ministry, which has been operating the airport, did not respond to questions from Reuters about suspected graves and land claims.
SANA cited the civil aviation authority's spokesperson as saying that Mezzeh's refurbishment would take into account the surrounding urban area and relevant legal and social issues, but did not specifically mention the graves or land rights. It is unclear who will develop the airport.
RESIDENTS PROTEST OVER LAND CLAIMS The dispute over the land on which airport facilities were built is decades old.
Under the Assads, private land was regularly expropriated for government projects, often without compensation.
Mezzeh airport was built on land belonging to hundreds of private citizens across 2.76 sq km (1.1 square miles), according to land records from the Moadamiya municipality shared with Reuters.
A former municipal official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters that expropriation decrees retroactively justified the government's use of those lands when the airport was built in 1956, and that compensation had not been paid.
Residents demonstrated in Moadamiya a day after the redevelopment plans were announced. “We welcome investment, but we should be sitting at the table and discussing our share with investors, not the state,” said one protest organiser, who gave his name as Abu Khaled. “We have a documented right to this land.”
The dispute comes as Syria faces calls to address Assad-era property seizures.
On September 2, United Nations land rights experts appealed to Syria's government to suspend and repeal laws they said had enabled systematic property dispossession under Assad, and to either establish mechanisms to return properties to their legitimate owners, or provide adequate compensation.

items.title: Trump arrives in Ireland to meet leaders before attending golf tournament
items.author: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Dublin on Saturday, where he will meet Ireland's leaders before attending a golf tournament at one of his resorts, a detour from his recent focus on the Iran war and his party's effort to maintain power in November's midterm elections.
items.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Dublin on Saturday, where he will meet Ireland's leaders before attending a golf tournament at one of his resorts, a detour from his recent focus on the Iran war and his party's effort to maintain power in November's midterm elections.
The meetings with Ireland's president and prime minister are not part of an official state visit. But coming after this week's Republican convention and the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, the talks could include politically sensitive topics such as economic issues and Irish leaders' concerns over the Iran war.
Trump is making his 48-hour foreign trip as his Republican Party campaigns to keep its majorities in both chambers of the U.S. Congress. The Iran conflict has heightened [USN:L6N44M0S0 TEXT:"economic concerns"] among American voters by raising gas prices nationwide.
He was greeted by Ireland's deputy prime minister and foreign minister on the tarmac at Dublin Airport.
Anti-war and anti-Trump protests are planned in Dublin and in western Ireland near the Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg.
Ireland is one of the European Union's [USN:L1N42309T TEXT:"most pro-Palestinian"] countries and passed a law in July curbing goods trade with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. U.S. lawmakers and the American ambassador to Ireland criticized the law.
U.S., IRELAND TIES Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin has so far avoided political flaps with the U.S.
"The relationship between Ireland and the United States is very important economically," Martin told reporters when asked about Trump's weekend trip. "It's very, very significant both ways."
U.S.-owned companies employ about 10% of workers in Ireland after successive governments [USN:L8N41412H TEXT:"prioritized"] their jobs and corporate tax revenue over decades, handing Ireland the healthiest public finances in Europe in recent years.
In Dublin on Saturday, Trump will meet Irish President Catherine Connolly, who was [USN:L8N3W10ZL TEXT:"elected"] head of state last year. When Trump last visited as president in 2019, Connolly, an outspoken politician with [USN:L8N3W50JH TEXT:"far-left views"] on foreign policy, protested outside Shannon Airport in western Ireland.
Some supporters have urged her to speak up against U.S. military actions around the world and defend Ireland's neutrality.
Including Trump, eight sitting U.S. presidents have visited Ireland, starting with John F. Kennedy in 1963. But this trip has some hallmarks of Trump's typical weekends, which often revolve around golf outings at his company's properties.
The Trump Organization took control in 2014 of the Doonbeg course, which is hosting the Irish Open golf tournament this weekend. Trump is expected to help present the trophy on Sunday to the tournament champion.

items.title: Back-to-back big innings propel Diamondbacks past Rangers
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado hit back-to-back homers in a five-run sixth inning, Ketel Marte doubled twice and drove in three runs and the Arizona Diamondbacks stopped the Texas Rangers 9-1 on Friday in Phoenix.
items.body:
Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado hit back-to-back homers in a five-run sixth inning, Ketel Marte doubled twice and drove in three runs and the Arizona Diamondbacks stopped the Texas Rangers 9-1 on Friday in Phoenix.
Gabriel Moreno had two hits and two RBIs and Ildemaro Vargas had two hits and drove in a run for the D-backs, who posted their major-league-best 44th comeback victory and have won five of their past six.
Carroll hit a two-run homer and Arenado followed in the sixth after Arizona knocked out Texas starter MacKenzie Gore (8-11) amid producing four runs and four doubles in the fifth.
Carroll, who missed the previous two games with lower back discomfort, broke a 5-for-48 slump with his 20th homer. Arenado hit his 24th.
Joc Pederson had two of Texas' five hits, with his RBI double giving the Rangers a 1-0 lead in the fifth off starter Merrill Kelly. Arizona's Kevin Ginkel (6-4) entered and got Brandon Nimmo to ground out with the bases loaded to end the inning.
Four Arizona relievers gave up three hits in 4 2/3 scoreless innings. Justin Martinez struck out the side on nine pitches in the sixth, the fifth immaculate inning in franchise history.
The D-backs (79-69) remained a half-game behind the San Diego Padres (79-68) for the final National League wild-card spot. Those two clubs are within striking distance of the NL wild-card leaders, the Philadelphia Phillies and Chicago Cubs (both 82-66).
The Rangers (72-76), who have lost five of seven, remained three games behind Houston (75-73) for the American League West lead and fell three games behind the Cleveland Guardians (75-73) for the final AL wild-card spot.
Arizona's Jordan Lawlar led off the fifth with a double. Ryan Waldschmidt walked, and Vargas doubled to tie the game. Marte followed with a two-run double for a 3-1 lead, chasing Gore. Facing Jakob Junis, Moreno singled in Marte.
Marte doubled home Waldschmidt in the sixth, and Moreno singled in Marte before Carroll's two-run homer and Arenado's shot capped the five-run inning.
Kelly gave up two hits and one run in 4 1/3 innings, with three walks and three strikeouts.
Gore was charged with four runs on five hits in four-plus innings, with two strikeouts and three walks.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Tiafoe proud of comeback season despite Shelton semi-final loss
items.author: Janina Rios
items.creator: Janina Rios
items.summary: Frances Tiafoe said learning to close out matches will be his next challenge after falling to compatriot Ben Shelton in the U.S. Open semi-finals on Friday, but the 11th seed left New York proud of a season that will lift him back into the world's top 10.
items.body:
Frances Tiafoe said learning to close out matches will be his next challenge after falling to compatriot Ben Shelton in the U.S. Open semi-finals on Friday, but the 11th seed left New York proud of a season that will lift him back into the world's top 10.
Tiafoe, appearing in his third U.S. Open semi-final, was unable to take the final step, falling to eighth seed [USN:L1N45401J TEXT:"Shelton 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5."]
Yet his run at Flushing Meadows guaranteed the 28-year-old will climb to a new career-high ranking of world number eight once the post-tournament rankings are released, returning him to the top 10 for the first time since 2023.
"It's been a great season for me, but also, you know, this one is tough," Tiafoe told reporters.

items.title: Rookies power Cardinals to win as White Sox's division lead shrinks
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Rookie Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal each had three hits and drove in two runs Friday night for the St. Louis Cardinals in a 7-3 victory against the visiting Chicago White Sox.
items.body:
Rookie Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal each had three hits and drove in two runs Friday night for the St. Louis Cardinals in a 7-3 victory against the visiting Chicago White Sox.
Alec Burleson had two hits and two RBIs for the Cardinals, whose own hopes remain dim in the National League wild-card race. The Cardinals (73-75) did manage to strike a blow against the first-place White Sox's chances of winning the American League Central.
Chase Meidroth hit a pair of home runs for Chicago, which had its division lead trimmed to a half-game over the second-place Cleveland Guardians (75-73), who beat the Minnesota Twins 5-2 on Friday. The White Sox (75-72) lost their fourth straight game.
Baez hit an RBI single against Anthony Kay to break a 2-2 tie in the third inning after Meidroth went deep in each of his first two at-bats against Matthew Liberatore. Meidroth has 14 home runs on the season.
The Cardinals added three runs in the fifth, with Burleson hitting an RBI single, Baez an RBI double and Bernal an RBI single for a 6-2 lead. Bernal also brought in Baez with a seventh-inning single.
Gordon Graceffo (8-1) entered in the fifth to get two outs in relief of Liberatore, who allowed two runs, six hits and three walks over 4 1/3 innings. Liberatore struck out two.
Kay (9-9) allowed three runs, five hits and a walk while fanning two over four innings. Trevor Richards gave up three runs in two innings.
Jordan Walker had two hits and two runs for St. Louis, which snapped a three-game losing streak. Closer Riley O'Brien pitched a 1-2-3 ninth inning in a non-save situation.
Randal Gricuk joined Meidroth in collecting two of Chicago's nine hits. Colson Montgomery went 0-for-4 with three strikeouts and a walk.
The White Sox have scored a combined eight runs in their losing streak, which began with a three-game sweep at the hands of the Pittsburgh Pirates.

items.title: テニス＝ズベレフが決勝進出、シェルトンは米国勢対決制す　全米ＯＰ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　１１日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　１１日　ロイター］ - テニスの四大大会最終戦、全米オープン（ＯＰ）は１１日、男子シングルス準決勝を行い、第１シードのアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）がロシア出身のカレン・ハチャノフを下し、決勝に進出した。

ズベレフは６─３、７─６、７─６のストレートで勝利し、自身２度目の四大大会制覇に王手をかけた。今年の全仏ＯＰを制したズベレフは、四大大会で３大会連続の決勝進出。全米ＯＰでは、２０２０年にドミニク・ティエム（オーストリア）に敗れて以来の決勝となる。

ズベレフは今大会、１回戦と２回戦でフルセットにもつれ込む接戦を強いられた。準決勝後には「２回戦後の午前３時ごろ、私とチームはロッカールームで、自分のプレーがいかに酷かったかを笑い合った。あのユーモアセンスに救われた」と振り返り、「少しは進歩したと思う。そうでなければ全米ＯＰの決勝には進出できていないだろう」と語った。

もう１試合は、第８シードのベン・シェルトンが第１１シードのフランシス・ティアフォーとの米国勢対決を制し、ズベレフが待つ決勝に進出した。第１セットを４─６で落としたシェルトンだが、第２セットから６─３、６─３、７─５と逆転し、自身初となる四大大会決勝に駒を進めた。

車いすの部では、男子シングルス準決勝で第１シードの小田凱人がマルティン・デラプエンテ（スペイン）に６─４、６─４で勝利。女子シングルス準決勝では上地結衣がアニク・ファンクート（オランダ）を７─５、６─０で下し、日本勢がともに決勝進出を決めた。

女子ダブルス決勝は上地、朱珍珍（中国）組が大谷桃子、郭珞瑶（中国）組に６─１、６─２のストレート勝ちで優勝した。

items.title: Antonio returns to English football with Watford move
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Watford have signed Michail Antonio on a free transfer on a one-year deal, bringing the former West Ham United forward back to English football.
items.body:
Watford have signed Michail Antonio on a free transfer on a one-year deal, bringing the former West Ham United forward back to English football.
The 36-year-old, West Ham's all-time leading Premier League goalscorer, was in a serious road accident in December 2024 when his car hit a tree on the way home from training. He broke his thigh bone in four places and did not play for the club again.
Antonio left West Ham in August 2025 after the London club opted not to renew his contract. They were relegated to the second-tier Championship after finishing 18th in the Premier League the last season.
He joined Qatari side Al-Sailiya in March, his first club since undergoing surgery following the accident.
"It's a good set of boys here," Antonio said in a statement on Friday. "They are focused and ready to show their abilities this season.
"Watford is a big club and hopefully I can come in and bring success and help wherever I can.
"I've scored a few goals against Watford! So hopefully I can score some for Watford now when I'm fully up to speed."
Watford are 12th in the Championship with eight points from six matches.
